title: Flow Velocity Gradient-Bounded Constitutive Theory of Incompressible Viscous Fluids
content: The incompressible Navier–Stokes equations have recently been shown to admit finite-time singularities from smooth data under smooth bounded forcing. Since unbounded velocity gradients are physically inadmissible, the only element of the equations open to revision is the constitutive relation $\sigma=-pI+F(\nabla u)$. From the Cauchy momentum equation we derive the most general $F$ compatible with frame indifference, isotropy and the Cayley–Hamilton theorem, $F=\alpha_1D+\alpha_2D\cdot D$ with invariant-dependent coefficients, and prove that the constant-coefficient second-order model $\sigma=-pI+2\mu D+4\lambda D\cdot D$ violates the second law in three dimensions, is an exact gradient in two, and cannot bound velocity gradients. The improvement must therefore enter the linear coefficient, and the lowest-order admissible law is $\sigma=-pI+2\mu(1+\tau^2 D: D) D+4\lambda\ D\cdot\ D$ with a material time $\tau$. We prove that the second law requires $\tau\ge|\lambda|/(\sqrt6\mu)$ and, by an exact block decomposition of the tangent operator, that monotonicity requires the sharp bound $\tau\ge\sqrt{2/3}\,|\lambda|/\mu$, twice the thermodynamic one. Under it the momentum operator is strongly monotone with quartic growth, the equations lie in the Ladyzhenskaya–Lions class $p=4$, solutions are global, unique and bounded, and the forced blow-up cannot occur. Exact solutions in simple shear and gravity-driven pipe flow give a two-measurement protocol for $\tau$ and $\lambda$ with an internal consistency test, and a strained vortex exhibits the arrest of collapse at strain rate $1/\tau$. A boundary-layer theory consistent to second order shows that $\lambda$ drops out exactly, that the flat-plate layer has a leading-edge regime $\delta\propto x^{1/4}$, $\tau_w\propto x^{-3/4}$ crossing over to Blasius scaling at $\ell_\tau=\tau^2U^3/(2\nu)$, and that only the wedge flow $U\propto x^{1/3}$ remains self-similar. Numerical solutions and experimental protocols are given.
